title: The Nyota Protocol
author: Natalie Wanjiru
content:
## Chapter One

The sky pulsed with electric blue grids, stretching across the floating city like veins of a living machine. Below, the Griot Market buzzed with activity—hackers trading stolen code, smugglers whispering deals, and drones weaving through the maze of neon-lit stalls.

Waceera pushed through the crowd, her heart hammering against her ribs. The encrypted file burned in her mind like a ticking bomb. She had barely cracked the first layer of its security when her bio-chip ID flashed red—she was flagged.

She ducked into a side alley, pressing against the damp wall. The city’s AI surveillance scanned everything, but she knew the backstreets better than most. Years of digging through Nairobi’s underbelly had taught her where the blind spots were.

Her earpiece crackled. “Waceera, you’ve got heat on you,” said Kimani, a rogue AI engineer and one of the last people she trusted. “I know,” she whispered. “How bad?”

“Bad.”

The digital billboard above flickered, and her face appeared on the screen. A red banner scrolled beneath it:

**WANTED: WACEERA – THREAT TO NATIONAL SECURITY**

Waceera cursed. They had activated the city-wide bounty system. She had only two minutes’ head start, and every merc and law enforcer in the county would be on her trail.

Then, she felt it. A shift in the air. A presence. She turned—too late. A sharp grip closed around her wrist, twisting her into a chokehold. A whisper, cold and precise, brushed against her ear.

“You should have deleted the file, Waceera,” said Njeri. Elite government operative. Program: Ndunge. Cyber-enhanced. Unstoppable.

Waceera struggled, but Njeri’s grip was steel. She dragged her into the shadows, away from the market’s chaos. The neon lights blurred as Waceera’s vision dimmed.

“This is it,” Waceera thought. “I’ve lost.”

Then—Kimani’s voice screamed through the earpiece. “Take a deep breath!”

A pulse erupted from Waceera’s wristband, disrupting Njeri’s bio-sync implants. The grip loosened. Waceera didn’t hesitate. She slammed her elbow into Njeri’s ribs, twisted free, and bolted.

She sprinted through the crowd, ducking beneath flying tuk-tuks and leaping over glowing fiber cables.

“Head for the old trainyard,” Kimani urged.

“Isn’t that out of range?”

“Exactly. They won’t expect you to go analog.”

Minutes later, breath ragged and muscles burning, Waceera dove into a rusted-out train shell buried beneath the city’s forgotten layers. Here, everything was off-grid. The perfect place to think—and to unlock the file.

She inserted the chip into Kimani’s scrambler. “Whatever’s in here,” she whispered, “It’s what they killed for.”

The file opened. And what she saw made her blood run cold:

**The Nyota Protocol wasn’t just surveillance. It was a rewrite code.**

A full system override, designed to erase the identities of anyone deemed a “threat to stability.” Names, history, memory—gone. A digital genocide.

The screen pulsed with coordinates: `ORACLE 01 – MT. ELGON BASE`

Waceera’s jaw tightened. “They want to rewrite us,” she said. “But I remember who we are.”

Kimani’s voice buzzed in. “Then let’s rewrite the ending.”

## Chapter Two

The train yard was cold and damp, a skeleton of Kenya’s pre-digital past. Rusted steel, vines creeping up ancient engines, and silence, blessed silence. For the first time in hours, Waceera let herself breathe.

Kimani’s voice broke the quiet. “You saw it, didn’t you?”

“Yeah,” Waceera said, her voice low. “It’s not surveillance. It’s extinction.”

She paced the floor of the train car, the screen flickering with fragments of code. The Nyota Protocol wasn’t just a threat—it had already begun. Some of the names on the deletion list… were people she knew. Activists. Historians. Indigenous knowledge-keepers.

“They’re erasing memory,” she whispered. “Culture. Resistance.”

Kimani hesitated.

“Waceera, I didn’t tell you everything. The Oracles—there’s a reason no one’s found them in years. They don’t just hide from the system… They left it.”

Waceera’s brow furrowed. “You mean—off-grid?”

“Beyond the code. Beyond the Cloud. They’re in the Rift. Analog minds with digital secrets.”

Suddenly, static cracked through the earpiece—then silence.

Waceera’s heart sank.

“Kimani?”

Nothing.

Then came the sound. Not static. Wings. Mechanical wings.

She dove to the floor just as a Hunter drone sliced through the train car’s roof with a laser. Sparks rained down. A red sensor light scanned the debris.

She ran.

Out of the train, through the ruins of old Nairobi. The sky above rippled satellite grids blinking into formation. The Nyota Protocol was adapting.

But she wasn’t alone.

In the shadows near a crumbled billboard, a figure stepped forward. Robes of dark ochre, beaded necklaces that glinted like circuitry, and a face etched with luminous white tribal lines.

“You are Waceera,” the figure said. Not a question. A knowing.

“Who are you?” she asked, backing away.

“I am Ajooni. Keeper of the Rift. You carry a memory the world wants to forget.”

Ajooni extended a hand. “Come. The Oracles are waiting.”

And with that, Waceera stepped off the map. Toward the mountain. Toward the truth. And deeper into the war for memory.

## Chapter Three

The Rift Valley stretched like a scar carved by forgotten gods. Crimson cliffs. Rolling mist. And silence that felt ancient.

Waceera followed Ajooni on foot. No drones here. No neon grids. The sky above was stars, not satellites.

“This place… It’s untouched,” she whispered.

“Not untouched,” Ajooni said. “Uncaptured.”

For hours, they hiked—through forests where the trees pulsed with ancestral tech, bark etched with digital glyphs. Streams whispered lost languages. It felt like stepping back in time and forward at once.

At dawn, they arrived.

Tucked into the cliffs of Mt. Elgon, hidden by sound-canceling stones and optical illusions, was the Oracle Sanctuary. A city of silence and memory. Elders sat in circles, wired to roots that glowed faintly. Youth trained in code, music, and martial forms born from ancient dances.

Waceera stared in awe. Ajooni bowed slightly. “These are the Oracles. The memory-keepers. The rebels of remembrance.”

One stepped forward—an older woman, her eyes milky, but glowing faintly. “You are the Daughter of Kanja,” she said.

Waceera froze. “How do you know that name?”

“Your mother saved one of us. Your father encoded part of the Protocol to warn us.”

The Oracles brought Waceera to the Memory Vault—a cave laced with vines and luminous script. A projection bloomed from the wall: President Mbappe, smiling, giving a speech.

“He says he's the reformer,” Ajooni muttered. “But he is Ndunge’s architect. A cyber-puppet.”

The truth unfolded.

Mbappe had been an intelligence officer during the Digital Conflicts. He used psychological warfare and data rewrites to crush rebellions. His greatest creation? The Nyota Protocol—disguised as a security system, designed to erase the roots of resistance.

But now, someone has cracked the first layer: Waceera.

“You are the anomaly,” Ajooni told her. “Your mind wasn’t raised in the system. That is your weapon.”

And she saw it. A way to disrupt the Protocol from the inside. To hijack Mbappe's next address—and broadcast the truth.

But it would mean war.

The Oracles handed her a small cube—an ancient chip from before the Cloud Age. “Inside is the last fragment of your father’s code. The key to the rewrite,” said the elder.

Waceera took it. Her hands trembled. From the cliffs above, she could see the satellite arrays glimmering like stars. She whispered:

**“It’s time to light the sky.”**

And below them, the Resistance stirred.
